historyIntro: Latest report per reporter in each UTC period. Missing reports are not carried forward. Opt-out removes past contributions too.
semantics: Usage means used at least once since schema consent, not activity in that period. Shares use only reporters that supplied the field; older schemas and configuration-only signals can be unknown.
error: Could not load data. Check your access and connection, then try again.
rangeError: Choose a valid range with at most 366 periods. Use weeks or months for longer ranges.
notCollected: Actual use is not collected for this capability. Select configuration to see its history.
dataIntro: Browse every reporter, inspect original reports and export all retained contributions: registration metadata, snapshots, reports, feedback, votes and operation receipts.
accessDisclosure: Who can read the data: participants can access shared aggregates and history, plus their own original reports. Maintainers can inspect and export all retained reporter contributions, including original reports and private feedback. This does not grant permission to publish private feedback. Opt-out removes the reporter’s data and historical contributions.
noPackets: This reporter has not sent a report yet.
workspaceIntro: Maintainers can access all retained usage contributions and cross-reporter history. Publishing feedback still requires the author’s permission. Access tokens stay in page memory.
inventorySemantics: Sum of each reporter’s last report in the period, including drafts and archived records. Videos are not photos. Missing values in older schemas are unknown; changes in reporting installations change the total.
inventorySummary: Sum of the latest report per reporter. No per-gallery breakdown, filenames or image contents.
inventoryCatalog: Totals describe currently stored database records, not upload activity or unique files. Thumbnails and videos are excluded from the photo total. Only these two numbers leave the installation.
distributionSemantics: Shares use only reporters that supplied the selected field. Missing or null fields are unknown; an empty layout list means no layouts reported.
downloadSignals: Allowed downloads (v2/v3) and restricted downloads (v4) are separate questions. Different galleries can make both true. Older values are never inverted or converted; missing values stay unknown.
catalogDisclosure: usage.v5: 64 configured/used pairs, 23 configuration-only signals, and the same two inventory totals. Built-in availability and enabled defaults do not prove use. Edit signals exclude unchanged saves and previews. Real template mail includes background sends and measures transport acceptance, not receipt or reading. Only fixed booleans; no contents, recipients, per-action times or frequencies.
catalogVersionDisclosure: v1–v4 retain their original scope and meaning. New edit/delivery signals begin only after explicit v5 consent. Old broad management questions remain separate in history. No observation since consent does not prove defaults or lifetime non-use. Missing values from older reporters stay unknown.
catalogConfigurationOnly: Configuration only — actual use is not collected.
adoptionIntro: See which features are configured and which have been used across participating installations. Based on each installation’s latest report.
adoptionSemantics: Use means an observation since consent, not frequency or recent activity. New editing signals exclude unchanged saves. No observed edit does not prove defaults; earlier customizations are unknown. Mail transport acceptance does not prove receipt or reading. Earlier, broader measurements remain separate.
adoptionUsedSomewhere: Features used by at least one installation
adoptionMajorityFeatures: Features used by more than half of those reporting
adoptionSortUsed: Ranked by share of installations using each feature
adoptionSortConfigured: Ranked by share of installations with each feature configured
adoptionEmpty: The overview will appear when an installation sends its first report.
adoptionNoMatches: No features match this view and search. Try another view or clear your search.
historyFilters: Explore history: dates, features and more
adoptionAvailabilityOnly: Available by design; this does not measure adoption.
loadFailure: We couldn’t load this data. Check your connection or access and try again.
lookupFailure: No participating installation matches this hash, or the service is unavailable. Deleted identities no longer have access.
lookupHelp: Found in PicPeak → Settings → Product usage & feedback. Read-only: it cannot vote, send reports, or delete data.
overviewIntro: Participating installations see which features help photographers most: the same data we use to decide what comes next.
participationMeta: Opt-in · Signed daily reports · Data for participants only
participantAccessIntro: Aggregate usage data is shown to participating installations, not to the public. Your lookup hash unlocks the dashboard, the dataset export and your own raw packets.
featureSignalsIntro: Each participating installation sends one signed daily report: which capabilities are configured and which were used, as yes/no. Feature signals and two inventory totals. No visitor tracking or names.
datasetVisibilityIntro: Participants see the whole dataset, including groups of one. That is why it is not published anonymously: the schema and the rules are public, the numbers belong to the people who contribute them.
publicRequestsIntro: Published feature requests and testimonials appear only with the author’s permission and can be read without signing in. Voting needs a connected PicPeak session.
capabilitySummary: Configuration / general capability use, never click counts
firstReportsTitle: The first reports will appear here.
firstReportsIntro: Enable product usage in PicPeak → Settings → Product usage & feedback. This dashboard shows accepted reports only; no sample installations are included.
layoutDisclosure: An installation can use several layouts. Per-layout gallery counts are never reported.
datasetIntro: Every feature combination is included, including groups of one. No installation hashes or signing keys are exposed. The full export is a consistent snapshot at its start time.
datasetPreviewIntro: One latest feature snapshot per reporting installation. The complete dataset is available above.
packetsIntro: Inspect each unique accepted usage report, exactly as first received. Transport retries are deduplicated; rejected attempts and separate feedback are not usage reports. The private lookup hash is read-only.
packetsAccessIntro: Enter the private lookup hash from PicPeak’s usage settings. It also unlocks the aggregate dashboard.
packetsFailure: No accessible installation was found, or the service is unavailable. Deleted identities no longer have access.
packetsDownloadIntro: The full download includes all accepted usage reports and a dated export receipt. Keep that file as your private audit record.
registeredWithoutReport: The installation is registered. Its first daily report has not arrived yet.
requestsTitle: A place for the next good idea.
requestsIntro: Read community requests and support the improvements that matter to you. Public requests appear only with the author’s permission and after maintainer review.
votingDuration: Your session lasts 15 minutes; opting out revokes it immediately.
votingConnectionHelp: Choose “Open usage portal” in your PicPeak usage settings. A lookup hash alone does not authorize votes.
submitFeedbackHelp: New requests and private feedback are submitted from the same PicPeak settings page.
noRequestsIntro: No feature requests have been approved for publication yet. Share yours from PicPeak’s feedback settings.
transparencyTitle: The rules are part of the product.
transparencyIntro: Participation is optional. The schema is public. Your raw packets and the aggregate dataset are inspectable by participants. Leaving deletes your contributions.
reportContentsIntro: A pseudonymous installation fingerprint, schema version, packet ID and sequence, signature metadata, PicPeak version, UTC report date, generation time, feature booleans, controlled gallery layout values, and (with v3, v4 or v5 consent) two installation totals: stored galleries and photo records excluding videos. Drafts and retained archived records are included.
signalMeaning: Configured means the capability is enabled or has relevant configuration; built-in capabilities mean available, not used. Used means a disclosed observation (usually a successful admin capability operation) since consent to the current schema. v1 measures since joining; explicitly upgrading the schema restarts local markers. It is a yes/no signal, never a frequency. Configuration-only fields omit used entirely.
schemaCompatibility: All five schema versions remain supported. Existing v1/v2/v3/v4 participants keep their previous scope until they explicitly consent to v5 in PicPeak. The current v5 catalog explains 87 capability signals and two inventory totals. New edit signals exclude unchanged saves and previews; template-mail use includes real background sends accepted by the mail transport, never test messages. Historical views preserve earlier broad editor measurements and the retired v2/v3 allowed-downloads question separately. Older and partial reports remain supported; omitted or null measurements are unknown.
layoutValues: Layouts: grid, masonry, carousel, timeline, mosaic, gallery-premium, gallery-story, or other. We never include the number of galleries using them.
excludedDataIntro: No gallery visitor tracking, clickstreams, per-gallery or per-photo breakdowns, image contents, biometric results, financial values, emails, domains, filenames, customer names, location, or configuration secrets in automatic reports.
networkPrivacy: The network sees an address to deliver a request. This application does not persist it in analytics or access logs. Abuse controls keep an ephemeral address HMAC in memory for ten minutes; IPv6 addresses share a /56 network budget before hashing.
participantVisibilityIntro: The aggregate dataset includes every reporting installation’s latest feature combination and results, including groups of one. It excludes installation fingerprints, raw signatures and private feedback. Rare combinations can still be distinctive: this is pseudonymous participation, not a promise of anonymity.
privateLookupDisclosure: That is why the numbers are not published anonymously. Your lookup hash unlocks the dashboard, the dataset export and all of your unique accepted usage reports while you participate. Keep it private. The schema, the rules, feature requests and testimonials stay public.
deletionIntro: Disable participation in PicPeak to stop collection immediately. PicPeak signs a deletion request; the collector deletes reports, projections, feedback, publications, votes, and sessions. The local key and hash are removed after confirmation. Outages leave deletion visibly pending and retryable.
revocationDisclosure: Only a one-way revocation digest remains to prevent old registrations from being replayed. It cannot retrieve a former installation’s data. A new opt-in generates a fresh identity. Short-lived global abuse counters contain no installation identity. Optional weekly reporting also retains identity-free join/opt-out totals for at most 90 days, as described below.
feedbackConsentIntro: Feedback is sent only when you submit it. You choose anonymity or a name per item. Private feedback is maintainer-only; feature requests and testimonials need your publication permission and review. Homepage marketing requires an additional explicit permission. Opt-out removes these items and their votes too.
signingIntro: PicPeak holds the Ed25519 private key on its backend and signs every operation. The collector checks the public-key fingerprint, schema, signature, timestamp, nonce, sequence and packet identity. Re-signed retries of the same packet are idempotent; reused nonces are rejected. Full copies of the same signing identity cannot be distinguished by cryptography alone: registration and sequence conflicts stop reporting and require review.
retentionIntro: Accepted raw reports are retained throughout active participation. Security nonces expire after ten minutes and voting sessions after fifteen. Cleanup runs at startup, on valid submissions and every minute. Tokens are never stored in operation receipts. Deletion removes active data and historical aggregate contributions. Signatures establish key ownership; they cannot attest that a self-hosted client runs unmodified software.
sourceIntroBefore: This service is developed as the separate
sourceContents: . The deployment includes the protocol, collector, UI, database migrations, tests, and operator documentation.
auditExportIntro: A report export contains each unique accepted usage report exactly as first received, with a dated receipt and report count. Re-signed transport retries are deduplicated; rejected attempts, registration, session commands and separate feedback are not usage reports. Dataset exports are consistent snapshots at export start. Already downloaded copies cannot be recalled by a later opt-out.
auditReceiptIntro: Download receipts to keep your own audit trail. PicPeak can show its latest local export receipt and identity-free deletion confirmation; opt-out clears the export receipt and all local identity/key material. The collector does not keep a personal export/access history. Receipts document acknowledgement, not forensic proof of storage erasure.
marketingFeedDisclosure: Homepage integrations use the marketing-approved testimonial feed, never the general portal testimonial list.
inboxEmptyIntro: Private and publication-requested feedback will appear here.
votingExpired: That voting connection has expired or is invalid. Open a new session from PicPeak.
notFoundIntro: Use the navigation to return to the community dashboard.
footerText: PicPeak Usage · MIT license · Opt-in, no visitor tracking
retentionRawReportsDuration: All logical reports while participating; deleted on opt-out.
retentionProjectionsDuration: While participating; committed deletion invalidates caches across replicas.
retentionFeedbackData: Feedback, names, publication/marketing choices and votes
retentionFeedbackDuration: Separate from telemetry; deleted on opt-out, including votes on deleted requests.
retentionOperationsData: Operation IDs, digests, dates and non-secret receipts
retentionOperationsDuration: While participating, for retries and quotas; deleted on opt-out. No bearer tokens.
retentionSessionsDuration: 15-minute validity, then the next cleanup cycle; never plaintext tokens.
retentionNoncesDuration: 10 minutes, then the next cleanup cycle.
retentionAdmissionDuration: Current and previous UTC day only, then cleanup; no identity or IP.
retentionRevisionDuration: Constant-size coordination state, with no identity history.
retentionRevocationsDuration: Persistent, to prevent old identities being registered again; no lookup access.
retentionAddressLimitsDuration: Process memory for ten-minute windows; no persistent IP, origin or user-agent.
retentionReceiptsDuration: Held by the requester; no central personal audit history. PicPeak keeps only the local latest receipts described above.
retentionInfrastructureDuration: No app access logger or automatic backup. Operators must disclose any separate backup retention, apply revocations on restore, and avoid payloads/credentials in logs; essential security logs should be kept at most 24 hours.
linkedFeedbackNotice: This link opens a specific message after maintainer sign-in.
linkedFeedbackMissing: This message is no longer available. It may have been removed when its author opted out.
weeklyEmailDisclosure: Operators can enable a weekly email for trusted maintainers containing aggregate usage insights and all new feedback, including private messages. Links require maintainer sign-in. Messages deleted before email preparation are excluded, but delivered email copies cannot be recalled. SMTP and mailbox retention are the operator’s responsibility.
weeklyCounterDisclosure: While enabled, the collector keeps only daily totals of new registrations and completed opt-outs for at most 90 days, without installation IDs, hashes, addresses or message contents. These aggregate operational counts survive individual opt-outs. Pending email receipts reference live feedback and are removed on opt-out or completion of that recipient’s weekly report. Disabling weekly reports clears the counters and delivery state.
retentionWeeklyData: Weekly email counts and delivery coordination
retentionWeeklyDuration: Aggregate joins/opt-outs: 90 days, without identity. Minimal per-recipient scheduling/retry state while enabled; feedback part receipts only until report completion or author opt-out. No email bodies stored by the scheduler. Disabling removes all of this state. Delivered mailbox copies remain with the maintainer.
